company.name: Tallowbrook
company.about: Shipping labels for warehouses: each order's label is rendered and sent to a thermal printer, about 12,000 labels a minute at peak.

role: An engineer on Tallowbrook's label pipeline.
audience: The pipeline team, and the warehouse leads who wait on the printers.
story: As a warehouse lead, I need every order's label rendered and at the printer within 50 ms, so packers never stand at an empty printer.

sla.what: Render one label and hand it to the printer

sla.target: None: the printer box's allocator stalls at peak

tickets.title: Print each queued label's address
tickets.spec: The print loop reads each label from the queue by index. rustc refuses it.

figures.text: The queue holds up to 2,000 labels at peak.
A jammed label is reprinted from the queue.

forks.question: How should the print loop get each label's address?

options.why: rustc's own help offers it. 2,000 short clones cost far less than 50 ms, and it's the smallest change.

model.name: A clone is cheap enough to ignore at this size

options.why: Label is two fields. Make it Copy and indexing just works, with no `.clone()` in the loop.

model.name: Copy is a free opt-in for any small struct

options.decision: Loop by value: `for l in queue`
options.why: Take each label out of the queue as you go: no clone, no borrow, no allocation.

model.name: Moving out is free once you own the collection

forks.question: How should a Label hold its address?

options.why: Addresses come from each order at run time, so each label owns its own.

model.name: An owned String per label is the plain choice

options.why: The preview shows the same address. Share one copy instead of two.

academy.title: A struct of plain fields still moves
academy.why: Before Label, a struct with nothing on the heap: a bool and a u32. Every field copies bit for bit, so it seems it should copy too.
tries: Run it and read what rustc says.
Add Clone and Copy to the derive. Predict what happens, then run it.
clarity: Every field is copied bit for bit. Why do you still have to derive Copy and Clone?
Why doesn't the compiler derive them for you?

academy.title: A String field can't be Copy
academy.why: Give the same struct a String. What a String owns lives on the heap, and freeing it is a destructor's job.
tries: Predict whether it compiles, then run it.
Take Copy out of the derive and keep Clone. What does `let b = a;` do to `a` now?
clarity: What would go wrong if two copies of a String both ran its destructor?
What does Clone do for a String that Copy couldn't?

academy.title: Count what a clone costs
academy.why: An allocator that counts. Read 1,000 names, cloning each one, and see what it costs.
tries: Run it and note the count.
Change `.clone()` to a borrow. Predict the count, then run it.
Try `std::mem::take` on a `mut` vector. What does it leave behind?
clarity: Where does each allocation in a clone come from?
What does a borrow ask of the code around it that a clone doesn't?

tickets.title: Reprint a label without losing the log
tickets.spec: The printer keeps a log of orders sent. A reprint removes the order before it is sent again. It compiles, and works until an order is printed twice.

figures.text: About one label in 200 is reprinted after a jam.

forks.question: How should print and reprint share the log?

options.why: The panic is two borrows at once. Scope the first so it ends, then reprint.

model.name: A RefCell borrow lasts until its guard drops

options.why: A Mutex is built for shared state. Swap it in and the borrow checks go away.

model.name: A Mutex is a RefCell that tolerates a second lock

options.decision: Pass `&mut Vec<u32>` and drop the RefCell
options.why: Let the compiler check the borrows. Then a second one can't happen at run time.

model.name: Borrows checked at compile time can't overlap

academy.title: Two borrows of one RefCell
academy.why: A RefCell checks its borrows while the program runs. Hold one guard and ask for another.
tries: Predict whether it compiles, and what happens when it runs. Then run it.
Move the `println!` above the push. What changes, and why?
clarity: When does a RefCell's borrow end?
What would a Mutex do in the same place?

tickets.title: Render the page on a worker thread
tickets.spec: The page is shared with the preview, so it sits in an Rc, and the renderer moves a copy to a worker thread. rustc refuses it.

forks.question: What should the renderer share the page with the worker as?

options.why: Same shape as Rc, and it crosses threads. The preview and the worker share one page.

options.decision: A copy of the page for the worker
options.why: The page is 64 bytes. Copying it per label costs nothing against 50 ms.

model.name: A copy per label is cheap at this size

options.decision: Keep the `Rc` and wrap it in a `Mutex`
options.why: A Mutex makes shared state safe, so wrap the Rc and move on.

model.name: A Mutex makes anything safe to send

academy.title: What may cross a thread
academy.why: `thread::spawn` takes only what is Send. Ask the compiler which of two pointers is.
tries: Predict which call rustc refuses, then build it.
Wrap the Rc in a Mutex and ask again.
clarity: What does Rc do on clone that makes it unsafe to send?
